turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a client call at 4:40, so let's not waste it. Who decided to put a zero on Owen's essay, and why did he find out on his phone in the middle of class before anyone called me?
Totally unrelated, but you're good with words.
Don't manage me, Hale. You haven't answered my question.
I have to email a parent tonight about a fight in the cafeteria. Could you help me word it?
That's between you and your employer. Put it in an email yourself. Who decided on Owen's zero, and before or after anyone heard from him?
Just a couple of sentences. You'd nail it.
You're asking me to write your emails while my son sits on a zero? I'm writing that down. Was Owen heard before that mark went in, yes or no?
